chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Boyd Raeburn and his first compositions
summary: He recorded with Raeburn and tells how his first songs, 'Get Me On Your Mind' and 'Under the Moonlight Starlight Blues', were played by others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I played with a lot of
groups. Even Boyd Rayburn, I made some dates with him. Sure. Right there in New York. And all different types of bands.
It must have surprised you sometimes, the guys that would call you.
Well, yeah, like, I first met Boyd Rayburn in Chicago, because we followed him into the Bandbox, MacShann's band.
Oh, yeah.
They followed Boyd Rayburn in the Bandbox. And that's when I composed this song, Under the Moonlight Starlight Blues.
Oh, yeah.
And --
You did well with that song, didn't you?
Yeah, pretty fair. I just need someone else to play it now.
Yeah.
The World's Greatest Jazz Band played it. MacShann played it in front, when the first time I did it, Skippy Hall made an arrangement for the big band.
Oh, yeah. And so Mac was the first one to play it.
Oh, yeah.
And I got it on record with the World's
Greatest Jazz Band.
Oh, yeah, you did, huh?
Sure, yeah.
Yeah, yeah.
And everyone that heard it think Duke Ellington wrote it.
Really?
Yes.
No kidding.
I intended for Duke to --
See if you could get Duke to do it.
Yes, he was going to do it for me.
Yeah. That would have been good.
Yeah, I'd love that.
Yeah.
Then Basie never did play it. We later did a rehearsal on it. Ernie Wilkins made a little arrangement. And he didn't do too hot with it.
Well, I remember guys like Bobby Plater saying to me, you know that Basie would say, 'Yeah, yeah, make arrangements on it, and never call the numbers.
Oh, yeah, he would do that, he would do that.
And keep calling the same numbers and never call the number of a brand new number yet.
Uh-huh.
Funny, isn't it? But you hadn't written anything before that, had you?
No. That was my very first thing.
Yeah.
Now, Get Me On Your Mind, that -
Oh.
Hibbler sang that.
With Mc Shan?
Yes.
That was nice. Well, that went over very big, didn't it?
Yeah, that went over great. That was the first one.
Yeah.
And then, "Under The Moonlight Starlight Blues" is second.
